# Figure 4 — The ≈10.63 circuit: real, specific, unexplained

**Generated by** `scripts/splicebert/make_fig4_carrier_circuit.py` from
`results/phase-lattice/fig_report_data.json`.

This figure separates **existence** from **interpretation**. The circuit exists. What it is for
is unknown, and the figure ends there.

## A — Eight heads in the corner, and in the human-only twin, none

Every head that clears the 2% attention-mass floor, plotted by post-softmax coherence **m_T** (x)
against the fraction of its attention pattern retained after the carrier is deleted (y). Point
size is the head's **attention mass in the tested offsets**; shade is layer.

The genuine readers occupy the **high-coherence / low-retention** corner: strongly locked to the
carrier, and largely destroyed when it is removed. In the multi-species checkpoint there are
**eight** of them. In its human-only twin — same estimator, same frozen gates, same 400
permutations, a model differing **only in training data** — there are **none**.

That contrast is the answer to the obvious objection. A blind instrument cannot find eight heads
in one model and zero in the other.

**There is no vertical significance line, and its absence is deliberate.** Significance is *not*
an m_T cutoff — it is BH-FDR over each head's **own** permutation null. Several heads with high
coherence are *not* significant, because their own spiky residual reproduces that coherence when
shuffled. Drawing a vertical threshold would tell a lie convenient to the story. Significance is
drawn as fill; the one genuine fixed threshold — the carrier-deletion collapse criterion, 0.50 —
is drawn as the dashed line.

## B — Carrier-dependent, content-independent

The four controls, for all eight Level-A heads. The signature is unusually clean:

| Condition | Pattern retained |
|---|---|
| **Carrier deleted** | **27–44%** — collapses |
| Reciprocal carrier deleted | 89–97% — survives |
| Low-leak band deleted | ~100% — survives |
| **Content shuffled** | **93–107%** — survives |

The last row is the one that matters most, and it is the one that is easiest to get backwards. A
positional comb **must** survive content shuffling. A pattern that vanished when the sequence was
scrambled would be a *content* artefact, not a positional circuit. These heads are reading
**position**, and nothing else.

**p-values are exact add-one permutation p-values**, floor 1/(400+1) = **0.0025**. They are never
printed as 0.0000, because 0 hits in 400 draws *bounds* a p-value, it does not measure one.
BH-FDR at q = 0.05 is applied across the whole scanned family (79 heads).

A limit of that budget, stated plainly: at 400 permutations, BH requires **≥ 4 heads at the
p-floor** before *any* head can be called significant. A lone reader would be undetectable here.
That is not what limits the human-only null — its best head has m_T = 0.001, and the
preregistered primary L1H3 puts only **0.19%** of its attention mass in the tested offsets, ten
times below the floor required even to enter the scan.

## C — Same neighbourhood, measurably different wavelengths, different evidence

Four things live near 10 nt, and conflating them has been the central risk of this whole project:

| | Wavelength | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| **Nucleosomal signal** | **10.298** | z = +249, depth 4.9%. Measured **in DNA**, not in the model. |
| **Multi-species carrier** | **10.630** | 8 post-softmax readers. **Level A.** |
| **Human-only component** | ≈10.17 | 0 of 14 preregistered readers. **Does not reach Level A.** |
| **Kogan splice phasing** | *unresolvable* | Real phenomenon; a 51-nt window has ΔT ≈ 4 nt at T = 10. |

The carrier and the nucleosomal signal differ by **0.33 nt**, and the carrier is fitted to
±0.005. **They are not the same wavelength**, and the multi-species carrier is therefore *not*
the measured nucleosomal periodicity. The upper tier shows why the Kogan phasing cannot arbitrate
this: at its coherence length the whole 7–16 nt scan is about two resolution elements wide, so its
peak is free to wander and cannot attribute anything.

## What remains open

The carrier's **origin** — biological, or an artefact of training dynamics — and its
**function** are both unresolved. Level A establishes that eight heads *read* it. It establishes
nothing about what they do with it, and this report does not speculate.
